About Nature CoNature Co delivers nature-based solutions (Nb S) for investors, corporates and other purpose driven organisations to scale up action on climate change and biodiversity loss. We specialise in nature-based project development including reforestation, agroforestry, farmer managed natural regeneration and mangrove restoration. Nature Co has extensive expertise in working with local communities to protect and restore natural ecosystems through participation in the global voluntary carbon market.Nature Co is currently implementing a large-scale reforestation project in Brazil for the generation of verified carbon credits.We are a diverse, mission-driven team that values inclusion, integrity, and innovation. Nature Co is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer, committed to building an equitable and inclusive workplace for all.Role and responsibilitiesThe Landholder and Reforestation Delivery Manager is the primary field-based interface with landholders, communities, reforestation contractors, and other local stakeholders for Nature Co’s projects in Brazil. This position will build and manage a pipeline of landholders interested in reforestation, lead outreach and onboarding, coordinate site inspections, lead the collection of relevant data required for carbon standard checks, and lead signature of landholder agreements. The role will also play a key role in ensuring compliance (contracts and carbon standards) as well as coordinate schedules between landholders and contractors for the implementation of reforestation activities. This will include confirming site readiness, conducting periodic field quality audits, documenting and tracking progress, and resolving issues that could delay delivery or degrade quality.The role requires a strong combination stakeholder engagement and management experience, and a commitment to quality and impact. The role requires extensive travel and field work across Minas Gerais, Bahia and Espírito Santo.Primary roles and responsibilities include:Landholder engagement, onboarding, and pipeline managementMap priority municipalities and referral partner networks (city governments, co-ops, farmer associations, NGOs); plan and run outreach activities, events and information sessions.Manage the landholder onboarding process (identify → qualify → onboard → contract), using CRM/trackers to keep status, documents and next actions current.Prepare clear information packs (benefits, obligations, timelines) and respond to inquiries in a timely, professional manner.Maintain ongoing landholder relationship management to support retention, satisfaction, and smooth site access throughout implementation.Eligibility, due diligence & agreementsCoordinate site inspections and initial diagnostics in consultation with other team members (parcel boundaries, vegetation status, access, water, risks).Support land tenure verification and FPIC documentationLead closure of contract signatures.Maintain organized repository of all landholder records within Nature Co’s data management system(land titles, eligibility documents, contracts, site maps, inspection notes, photos, consultation records).Reforestation delivery enablementTranslate signed landholder agreements into implementation-ready site plans (site-specific scope, access instructions, constraints, schedule windows).Align field schedules with landholders and contractors to ensure access, minimize disruption to farm activities, and maintain trust and cooperation.Support in the delivery of field delivery progress from contractors by site (start/finish dates, activities completed, challenges, next steps), and escalate issues early (access, weather delays, input shortages, labor constraints).Support in monitoring reforestation activities (during and post planting) and coordinate, where required, rapid response with contractors/landholders (grazing, fire risk, pests, drought stress).Stakeholder engagement and safeguardsPlan and document stakeholder consultations and community meetings in accordance with Nature Co policies and procedures (agendas, attendance lists, minutes, photos).Support the team in the operation of the grievance mechanism: receiving grievances and responding in accordance with the Nature Co grievance mechanism.Maintain landholder contact and ensure landholder information is kept up to date.Coordinate access, for other project staff and contractors as required.ReportingLead or assist the development of formal monthly, quarterly, and annual project implementation reports for internal and external stakeholders in line with contract and/or carbon standard requirements.Prepare ad hoc reports, documents, and presentations for internal and external stakeholders.Teamwork and cultureSupport the management of a cross-functional, international team, fostering collaboration and ensuring that project milestones and goals are met.Stay current on emerging best practices in Nb S and carbon projects; proactively share insights across the organisation and with partners.Skills and attributesTo perform successfully in this role, you will have:A minimum of five (5) years of experience in reforestation projects with direct contact with rural landholders and reforestation planting service providers.Degree in forest engineering, agronomy, ecology, or environmental science.Intermediate English and native Portuguese language skillsExcellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage confidently across cultures and stakeholder groups.Strong project management skills, including experience managing timelines, deliverables, and working across multidisciplinary teams.A proactive, self-starting approach with the ability to anticipate problems, adapt quickly, and take initiative under limited supervision.A collaborative mindset and ability to lead and motivate internal teams and external partnersAbility to provide strategic and technical guidance across complex, multi-stakeholder projects.Strong organisational skills and attention to detail in documentation and reporting.A positive, energetic personality with resilience and drive to see projects through to delivery.Extensive travel within Brazil is a requirement to perform this position.LocationRemote, with residence in Minas Gerais, Espirito Santo, or BahiaSubmission instructionsEmail CV and brief cover letter to with subject: Landholder and Reforestation Delivery ManagerSubmission deadline: 30 March 2026

title: Landholder and reforestation delivery manager
description:
Nova oportunidade para Landholder and reforestation delivery manager em campo bom. Saiba mais sobre essa vaga.

About Nature CoNature Co delivers nature-based solutions (Nb S) for investors, corporates and other purpose driven organisations to scale up action on climate change and biodiversity loss. We specialise in nature-based project development including reforestation, agroforestry, farmer managed natural regeneration and mangrove restoration. Nature Co has extensive expertise in working with local communities to protect and restore natural ecosystems through participation in the global voluntary carbon market.Nature Co is currently implementing a large-scale reforestation project in Brazil for the generation of verified carbon credits.We are a diverse, mission-driven team that values inclusion, integrity, and innovation. Nature Co is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer, committed to building an equitable and inclusive workplace for all.Role and responsibilitiesThe Landholder and Reforestation Delivery Manager is the primary field-based interface with landholders, communities, reforestation contractors, and other local stakeholders for Nature Co’s projects in Brazil. This position will build and manage a pipeline of landholders interested in reforestation, lead outreach and onboarding, coordinate site inspections, lead the collection of relevant data required for carbon standard checks, and lead signature of landholder agreements. The role will also play a key role in ensuring compliance (contracts and carbon standards) as well as coordinate schedules between landholders and contractors for the implementation of reforestation activities. This will include confirming site readiness, conducting periodic field quality audits, documenting and tracking progress, and resolving issues that could delay delivery or degrade quality.The role requires a strong combination stakeholder engagement and management experience, and a commitment to quality and impact. The role requires extensive travel and field work across Minas Gerais, Bahia and Espírito Santo.Primary roles and responsibilities include:Landholder engagement, onboarding, and pipeline managementMap priority municipalities and referral partner networks (city governments, co-ops, farmer associations, NGOs); plan and run outreach activities, events and information sessions.Manage the landholder onboarding process (identify → qualify → onboard → contract), using CRM/trackers to keep status, documents and next actions current.Prepare clear information packs (benefits, obligations, timelines) and respond to inquiries in a timely, professional manner.Maintain ongoing landholder relationship management to support retention, satisfaction, and smooth site access throughout implementation.Eligibility, due diligence & agreementsCoordinate site inspections and initial diagnostics in consultation with other team members (parcel boundaries, vegetation status, access, water, risks).Support land tenure verification and FPIC documentationLead closure of contract signatures.Maintain organized repository of all landholder records within Nature Co’s data management system(land titles, eligibility documents, contracts, site maps, inspection notes, photos, consultation records).Reforestation delivery enablementTranslate signed landholder agreements into implementation-ready site plans (site-specific scope, access instructions, constraints, schedule windows).Align field schedules with landholders and contractors to ensure access, minimize disruption to farm activities, and maintain trust and cooperation.Support in the delivery of field delivery progress from contractors by site (start/finish dates, activities completed, challenges, next steps), and escalate issues early (access, weather delays, input shortages, labor constraints).Support in monitoring reforestation activities (during and post planting) and coordinate, where required, rapid response with contractors/landholders (grazing, fire risk, pests, drought stress).Stakeholder engagement and safeguardsPlan and document stakeholder consultations and community meetings in accordance with Nature Co policies and procedures (agendas, attendance lists, minutes, photos).Support the team in the operation of the grievance mechanism: receiving grievances and responding in accordance with the Nature Co grievance mechanism.Maintain landholder contact and ensure landholder information is kept up to date.Coordinate access, for other project staff and contractors as required.ReportingLead or assist the development of formal monthly, quarterly, and annual project implementation reports for internal and external stakeholders in line with contract and/or carbon standard requirements.Prepare ad hoc reports, documents, and presentations for internal and external stakeholders.Teamwork and cultureSupport the management of a cross-functional, international team, fostering collaboration and ensuring that project milestones and goals are met.Stay current on emerging best practices in Nb S and carbon projects; proactively share insights across the organisation and with partners.Skills and attributesTo perform successfully in this role, you will have:A minimum of five (5) years of experience in reforestation projects with direct contact with rural landholders and reforestation planting service providers.Degree in forest engineering, agronomy, ecology, or environmental science.Intermediate English and native Portuguese language skillsExcellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage confidently across cultures and stakeholder groups.Strong project management skills, including experience managing timelines, deliverables, and working across multidisciplinary teams.A proactive, self-starting approach with the ability to anticipate problems, adapt quickly, and take initiative under limited supervision.A collaborative mindset and ability to lead and motivate internal teams and external partnersAbility to provide strategic and technical guidance across complex, multi-stakeholder projects.Strong organisational skills and attention to detail in documentation and reporting.A positive, energetic personality with resilience and drive to see projects through to delivery.Extensive travel within Brazil is a requirement to perform this position.LocationRemote, with residence in Minas Gerais, Espirito Santo, or BahiaSubmission instructionsEmail CV and brief cover letter to with subject: Landholder and Reforestation Delivery ManagerSubmission deadline: 30 March 2026

This position will build and manage a pipeline of landholders interested in reforestation, lead outreach and onboarding, coordinate site inspections, lead the collection of relevant data required for carbon standard checks, and lead signature of landholder agreements. The role will also play a key role in ensuring compliance (contracts and carbon standards) as well as coordinate schedules between landholders and contractors for the implementation of reforestation activities. This will include confirming site readiness, conducting periodic field quality audits, documenting and tracking progress, and resolving issues that could delay delivery or degrade quality.The role requires a strong combination stakeholder engagement and management experience, and a commitment to quality and impact. The role requires extensive travel and field work across Minas Gerais, Bahia and Espírito Santo.Primary roles and responsibilities include:Landholder engagement, onboarding, and pipeline managementMap priority municipalities and referral partner networks (city governments, co-ops, farmer associations, NGOs); plan and run outreach activities, events and information sessions.Manage the landholder onboarding process (identify → qualify → onboard → contract), using CRM/trackers to keep status, documents and next actions current.Prepare clear information packs (benefits, obligations, timelines) and respond to inquiries in a timely, professional manner.Maintain ongoing landholder relationship management to support retention, satisfaction, and smooth site access throughout implementation.Eligibility, due diligence & agreementsCoordinate site inspections and initial diagnostics in consultation with other team members (parcel boundaries, vegetation status, access, water, risks).Support land tenure verification and FPIC documentationLead closure of contract signatures.Maintain organized repository of all landholder records within Nature Co’s data management system(land titles, eligibility documents, contracts, site maps, inspection notes, photos, consultation records).Reforestation delivery enablementTranslate signed landholder agreements into implementation-ready site plans (site-specific scope, access instructions, constraints, schedule windows).Align field schedules with landholders and contractors to ensure access, minimize disruption to farm activities, and maintain trust and cooperation.Support in the delivery of field delivery progress from contractors by site (start/finish dates, activities completed, challenges, next steps), and escalate issues early (access, weather delays, input shortages, labor constraints).Support in monitoring reforestation activities (during and post planting) and coordinate, where required, rapid response with contractors/landholders (grazing, fire risk, pests, drought stress).Stakeholder engagement and safeguardsPlan and document stakeholder consultations and community meetings in accordance with Nature Co policies and procedures (agendas, attendance lists, minutes, photos).Support the team in the operation of the grievance mechanism: receiving grievances and responding in accordance with the Nature Co grievance mechanism.Maintain landholder contact and ensure landholder information is kept up to date.Coordinate access, for other project staff and contractors as required.ReportingLead or assist the development of formal monthly, quarterly, and annual project implementation reports for internal and external stakeholders in line with contract and/or carbon standard requirements.Prepare ad hoc reports, documents, and presentations for internal and external stakeholders.Teamwork and cultureSupport the management of a cross-functional, international team, fostering collaboration and ensuring that project milestones and goals are met.Stay current on emerging best practices in Nb S and carbon projects; proactively share insights across the organisation and with partners.Skills and attributesTo perform successfully in this role, you will have:A minimum of five (5) years of experience in reforestation projects with direct contact with rural landholders and reforestation planting service providers.Degree in forest engineering, agronomy, ecology, or environmental science.Intermediate English and native Portuguese language skillsExcellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage confidently across cultures and stakeholder groups.Strong project management skills, including experience managing timelines, deliverables, and working across multidisciplinary teams.A proactive, self-starting approach with the ability to anticipate problems, adapt quickly, and take initiative under limited supervision.A collaborative mindset and ability to lead and motivate internal teams and external partnersAbility to provide strategic and technical guidance across complex, multi-stakeholder projects.Strong organisational skills and attention to detail in documentation and reporting.A positive, energetic personality with resilience and drive to see projects through to delivery.Extensive travel within Brazil is a requirement to perform this position.LocationRemote, with residence in Minas Gerais, Espirito Santo, or BahiaSubmission instructionsEmail CV and brief cover letter to with subject: Landholder and Reforestation Delivery ManagerSubmission deadline: 30 March 2026

title: Strategic partnership & alliance
description:
Confira a vaga para Strategic partnership & alliance em sumaré. Veja os detalhes e como se candidatar.

About Rate GainRate Gain Travel Technologies Limited is a global provider of AI-powered Saa S solutions for travel and hospitality that works with 3,200+ customers and 700+ partners in 100+ countries helping them accelerate revenue generation through acquisition, retention, and wallet share expansion. Rate Gain today is one of the world’s largest processors of electronic transactions, price points, and travel intent data helping revenue management, distribution and marketing teams across hotels, airlines, meta-search companies, package providers, car rentals, travel management companies, cruises and ferries drive better outcomes for their business.Founded in 2004 and headquartered in India, today Rate Gain works with 26 of the Top 30 Hotel Chains, 25 of the Top 30 Online Travel Agents, 4 of the Top 5 Airlines, and all the top car rentals, including 16 Global Fortune 500 companies in unlocking new revenue every day.Exploring the roleRate Gain is privileged to partner with hotels of every size and type around the world to achieve their commercial objectives – from independent, luxury, lifestyle, and boutique hotels, to the world’s largest chains. Chains - and multi-site operators - have unique business requirements, additional complexity, and often use more diverse technology solutions. As a partner of choice for global and regional chains, Rate Gain is looking to further serve this important segment of the hospitality industry and seeks an experienced Director focused on European markets, to further scale this essential unit of our business.The ideal candidate will understand how Latam hotel chains function and operate, and will be familiar with the technology solutions adopted by these chains to achieve their commercial objectives. The role requires a trusted advisor, able to assist chains to manage through the complexities of the travel technology eco system to guide them to the right decisions in the areas of distribution, business intelligence, marketing technologies, and beyond.This is an individual contributor role and, as such, the candidate is expected to be a self-started and self-driven, ready to innovate to find new values for our hotel chain clients whilst keeping the company goals and the bigger picture firmly in mind. This position can be based anywhere in Latam and needs to have the ability to travel within the Latam without limitations.How your day will look like/Job responsibilityBuild and manage strategic alliances with regional and local partners (e.g. RMS, PMS, booking engines, OTAs)Define and execute a partnership roadmap aligned with Rate Gain’s GTM strategy in LATAMIdentify co-marketing, co-selling, and integration opportunities with key players in the hospitality and travel ecosystemCollaborate with internal teams (Sales, Marketing, Product, Legal) to structure and execute partnership agreementsRepresent Rate Gain in industry events and partnership meetings to promote our brand and solutionsMonitor partner performance, engagement, and contribution to pipeline and revenueProvide regular reporting and insights on partnership outcomes and market trendsEducation & Work ExperienceBachelor’s degree in business, Marketing, or a related field5+ years of experience in business development or strategic partnershipsKnowledge:In-depth understanding of the LATAM hospitality and travel technology ecosystemKnowledge of Saa S business models and partnership structuresAwareness of regional trends, customer behavior, and competitive landscape in the travel and hospitality sectorsSkills:Strong negotiation and deal-closing capabilitiesExcellent relationship management skills with ability to engage partners at all levelsAdvanced verbal and written communication skills inSpanish, Portuguese, and EnglishAbility to identify, pitch, and convert strategic partnership opportunitiesProficiency in using CRM and sales enablement toolsSkilled in cross-functional collaboration with internal teams (Sales, Marketing, Legal, Product, etc.)Attitude:Proactive and results-oriented, with a strong drive to exceed targetsEntrepreneurial mindset with a passion for growth and innovationCulturally sensitive and collaborative, with the ability to work effectively in a global, remote teamHigh level of integrity, professionalism, and ownershipResilient and adaptable in a fast-paced and evolving environment
